The method is also featured in Godot's volumetric rendering pipeline, as described in research on temporal anti-aliasing for real-time froxel-based volumetric rendering [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method is featured in Godot's volumetric rendering pipeline as described in research on temporal anti-aliasing for real-time froxel-based volumetric rendering [S1]. The provided evidence from Source [S1] explicitly details the 'modified Godot volumetric rendering pipeline' and describes multiple shader passes (Pass 1 through Pass 6) that implement Temporal Anti-Aliasing (TAA) techniques (such as reprojection, jittering, blending with history, and low-pass filtering) for 'froxel-based' rendering. The text confirms that these techniques are implemented within the Godot engine and are part of the research described in [S1].
supported

Unlike [Voxel Cone Tracing](1454-voxel-cone-tracing.md) which relies on cone tracing for indirect lighting, or [Precomputed Lighting (Baking)](2169-precomputed-lighting-baking.md) which uses static data, this method computes dynamic in-scattered radiance and shadows per froxel, often combined with [Froxel TAA Reprojection](1920-froxel-taa-reprojection.md) to stabilize temporal noise [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method computes dynamic in-scattered radiance and shadows per froxel, often combined with Froxel TAA Reprojection to stabilize temporal noise. Source [S1] confirms that Pass 1 evaluates 'in-scattered lighting by iterating light sources (accumulating radiance with shadow maps...)' and Pass 2 is a 'TAA Resolve' pass that blends newly sampled radiance with reprojected historical values to handle temporal stability (implied by the context of TAA and jittering). The claim accurately reflects the processes described in the evidence.

Froxel-based Volumetric Rendering is a real-time approximation for light transport in participating media that amortizes ray-queried occlusion lighting work by dividing the camera view frustum into a 3D grid of voxels ("froxels") [S2, unofficial].

The claim states that Froxel-based Volumetric Rendering is a real-time approximation for light transport in participating media that amortizes ray-queried occlusion lighting work by dividing the camera view frustum into a 3D grid of voxels ('froxels'). Source [S2] explicitly confirms this by describing the implementation as 'Wronski/Frostbite-style frustum-aligned volumetric fog (froxels)' and stating that 'Lighting work is done once per froxel (amortized ray-queried occlusion) instead of per-pixel per step'. It further details the grid structure ('XY is a screen tile footprint and Z is an exponential depth distribution') and the goal of delivering 'spatial-accumulation savings' through this amortization. All specific facts in the claim are present and supported by the evidence.
supported
